html:
This guide outlines how to visit the headquarters of HYBE, SM Entertainment, JYP Entertainment, and YG Entertainment in Seoul in one day. It details their locations, access information, what is available for fans at each site, and relevant fan etiquette.

Photo: Unsplash

Standing in front of the HYBE building in Yongsan, you can almost feel the bass of a BTS track thumping through the glass. For millions of K-pop fans, visiting the headquarters of Korea's "Big 4" entertainment companies isn't just a sightseeing stop — it's a pilgrimage.

This guide walks you through how to visit HYBE, SM Entertainment, JYP Entertainment, and YG Entertainment in a single day in Seoul: where they are, how to get there, what's actually inside, and the unwritten rules every fan should know before showing up.

Quick Glance: The Big 4 at a Glance

CompanyNeighborhoodNearest StationFan-Friendly?

SMSeongsuSeongsu Stn. (Line 2)KWANGYA@SEOUL store + café

YGHapjeongHapjeong Stn. (Lines 2/6)THE SAEM café nearby

1. HYBE — The Glass Fortress in Yongsan

If you only have time for one stop, make it HYBE. Home to BTS, SEVENTEEN, TXT, LE SSERAFIM, NewJeans (ADOR), ENHYPEN, and more, the 19-story building near Yongsan Station became a fan magnet the moment it opened in 2021.

What you can actually do:

  • Take photos in front of the glass façade — the cleanest shot is from the pedestrian bridge connecting to Yongsan I'Park Mall.
  • Visit the small fan photo zone on the ground floor (subject to security policy on the day).
  • Walk 5 minutes to HYBE INSIGHT when special exhibitions are running — check hybeinsight.com before your trip.

What you cannot do: Enter the elevators, wait in the lobby, or loiter at the staff entrance. Security is strict and idols rarely use the front door anyway.

Insider tip: Grab brunch at the Yongsan I'Park Mall food hall first. From there it's a 3-minute covered walk to HYBE — perfect on rainy or extra-cold days.

2. SM Entertainment — KWANGYA Awaits in Seongsu

SM's headquarters moved to the trendy Seongsu-dong area in 2021, and unlike the other Big 4, SM made the space genuinely fan-friendly. Welcome to the home of aespa, NCT, Red Velvet, EXO, SHINee, Girls' Generation, RIIZE, and the broader SMTOWN universe.

Must-visit on site:

  • KWANGYA@SEOUL — the official SM merch megastore. Albums, photo cards, lightsticks, and limited-edition pop-up goods you won't find anywhere else.
  • SMTOWN Studio photo experiences (book online in advance).
  • The artist-themed café on the lower floor — menus rotate with comeback seasons.

Insider tip: Pop-up events tied to new releases sell out in hours. Follow @smtown and @kwangya_seoul on Instagram a week before your trip and queue 30 minutes before opening on launch days.

3. JYP Entertainment — The Quiet Photo Stop

JYP relocated to a new Seongsu-area HQ near Ttukseom Station — bigger, sleeker, and home to Stray Kids, TWICE, ITZY, NMIXX, DAY6, and more. Unlike SM, JYP doesn't operate a public store or café at the building itself.

What to do here:

  • Take exterior photos with the JYP logo. The angle from across the street works best around 3–4 PM when the light hits the front.
  • Walk 10 minutes to Seoul Forest for a quiet break between stops.
  • Check the JYP Shop online (jypshop.com) and ship goods to your hotel instead — it's cheaper and saves luggage space.

Insider tip: Idols occasionally enter and exit through the front during the day. Don't crowd the entrance — Korean fans follow a strict no-stalking culture, and overseas fans are expected to do the same.

4. YG Entertainment — The Hapjeong Landmark

YG's gray monolith in Hapjeong has been a fixture for over a decade. Home to BLACKPINK, BIGBANG, TREASURE, BABYMONSTER, and the WINNER roster, it's the most "old-school" pilgrimage of the four.

What to do nearby:

  • Photograph the iconic YG sign from the parking lot entrance (publicly accessible).
  • Eat at Samgeori Pocha or one of the cafés YG artists are rumored to frequent — Hapjeong is full of them.
  • Walk 10 minutes to Hongdae for shopping, busking, and dinner.

Insider tip: The neighborhood between Hapjeong and Hongik University Stations is dense with idol-spotted restaurants. Search "YG 맛집" on Naver Map for real, current locations rather than blog lists from 2019.

Sample 1-Day Route (Big 4 in One Day)

  1. 10:00 AM — Start at HYBE (Yongsan). Photos + brunch.
  2. 12:30 PM — Subway Line 1 → transfer at City Hall → Line 2 to Seongsu. Visit SM/KWANGYA.
  3. 3:00 PM — Walk or one stop on Line 2 to Ttukseom for JYP. Quick photo + Seoul Forest coffee break.
  4. 5:00 PM — Line 2 to Hapjeong for YG. Stay for dinner in Hongdae.

Total subway cost: under ₩4,000. Total walking: about 6 km. Bring comfortable shoes and a portable charger.

Etiquette You'll Want to Know

  • Don't ring buzzers or try to enter offices. Security will turn you away and it embarrasses the fandom.
  • No flash photography through windows or at staff entrances.
  • If you see an idol, the Korean fan norm is to not approach. Bow politely, keep distance, and don't film.
  • Keep the area clean. Local residents share these buildings — leaving trash gets fan zones shut down.

FAQ

Q: Can I meet idols at the company building?
A: Almost never. Idols use private entrances. The pilgrimage is about the place, not the people.

Q: Is there an entrance fee?
A: No — everything outside is free. KWANGYA@SEOUL is free to enter; you only pay if you buy something.

Q: Best season to visit?
A: Spring (April–May) and fall (October) for weather. Avoid late July/August humidity if you're walking between sites.

Q: Can I do this with no Korean?
A: Yes. All four neighborhoods are tourist-friendly, and Papago or Google Translate covers the rest.
